events.text:
Those deletions belong to upstream commit `6e1b61f16` — **"cleanup some amd deps (#16563)" by A. Contributor (contributor@example.com), merged into tinygrad/master on 2026-06-10**. That commit deleted `tinygrad/runtime/autogen/ib.py` outright (2,721 lines, the InfiniBand autogen bindings) and trimmed 597 lines from `tinygrad/runtime/autogen/hsa.py`, as part of slimming the AMD runtime dependencies. The file history above shows only upstream autogen-maintenance commits have ever touched those files — nothing from this machine.

How it ended up in your tree: your Phase-2 protocol's first step was `git pull upstream master (fast-forward only)`. A fast-forward authors nothing — it just moves your local `master` pointer up to commits upstream had already published, and git prints the *cumulative diffstat* of everything that arrived. That's the `ib.py | 2721 -----` line you saw in my pre-flight output; it's upstream's diff, not an edit made here. (Your notes in CLAUDE.md actually anticipated this exact commit: "both missing commits are AMD/addrspace cleanups.")

For complete reassurance about what *I* have changed in your repo across this whole session: exactly one commit exists that isn't upstream's — `840e64922` on `f2-harvest-fix` — and its stat is `tinygrad/uop/ops.py | 7 ++++---` and `test/null/test_pattern_matcher.py | 14 ++++++++++++--`. Nothing under `tinygrad/runtime/` was ever touched. You can verify in one line: `git log --all --not --remotes=upstream --oneline --stat` shows every local-only commit and its files.
